findings.evidence: `pkg/owner/manager.go:184` creates a force-owner session and retries `tryToBeOwnerOnce`; `pkg/owner/manager.go:208` retries but `pkg/owner/manager.go:218` always returns nil, discarding the last error. `pkg/owner/manager.go:225`, `pkg/owner/manager.go:250`, `pkg/owner/manager.go:261` show `tryToBeOwnerOnce` can fail on etcd Get/Txn/Campaign(timeout). `pkg/ddl/ddl.go:766` enters upgrade mode and `pkg/ddl/ddl.go:772` expects `ForceToBeOwner` to return an error to abort. `pkg/session/session.go:3719` starts domain with upgrade startMode and `pkg/session/session.go:3736` proceeds to `upgrade(s)` after a fixed sleep regardless of whether forcing owner actually succeeded.
findings.fix: Propagate failure when retries are exhausted, e.g. after the retry loop `if err != nil { return errors.Trace(err) }`. Consider also using the passed-in ctx (instead of ignoring it) so callers can bound force-owner time, and (optionally) add a post-condition check (e.g. verify this session’s campaign key is present / verify elected owner ID) before returning success.
findings.impact: In upgrade startMode, TiDB can continue bootstrapping/upgrading even if the “force to be owner” operation repeatedly fails (etcd errors, txn op limits, campaign timeout due to concurrent keys). That undermines the stated invariant that upgrade-related DDLs run on the new-version node, and can lead to: (1) upgrade DDL jobs being executed by an older-version DDL owner, (2) upgrade hanging due to no stable owner, or (3) larger multi-owner windows during election churn—risking metadata/state-machine inconsistencies.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `pkg/owner/manager.go:179` still returns nil unconditionally after the retry loop (`pkg/owner/manager.go:209`).
findings.verify: Add a focused unit/integration test that forces `tryToBeOwnerOnce` to fail (e.g. inject etcd txn failure / campaign timeout) and assert `ForceToBeOwner` returns non-nil and `ddl.Start(Upgrade, ...)` fails fast; also validate a rolling-upgrade scenario where other nodes campaign concurrently and ensure upgrade does not proceed unless forcing owner succeeds.
findings.what: `ForceToBeOwner` swallows errors after retries (always returns nil), so upgrade-mode startup can proceed even when “force to be owner” did not succeed.
